clue.text: Are you having me on the crag rocks?

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climber, told something unlikely on a cliff face, asks whether they are being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: GERTCHA is London (Cockney) slang, a contraction of 'get away with you', said in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang exclamation expresses disbelief, the same as asking whether someone is teasing you.

clue.text: Large sum borne by 14 city with industrial action

indicators.note: in a down clue, borne by means carried on top of, so it comes first

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
the clue at 14 points to a northern European, and Oslo is a city in Norway

explanation.surface: A city with a big sum of money is hit by strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a protest where workers deliberately work slowly, a form of industrial action.

clue.text: Right about improvised flexibility of tempo

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician correctly describing improvised loosening of the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is a musical term for freely speeding up and slowing down within a phrase.

clue.text: It looks just the same as small engine part and performing ape

parts.note: carb is short for carburettor
on means on stage, performing
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: Something identical to a tiny engine component and a circus ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon copy is an exact duplicate, identical in appearance.

clue.text: A model, upwardly mobile Greek writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: An ambitious model who is also an ancient Greek author.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the fables.

clue.text: Not a nomad liked by creditors

definitions.meaning: someone who has made a permanent home in one place
someone who pays off what they owe, which pleases those owed money

explanation.surface: A description of a stay-at-home person who also pays their bills on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist who stays put and a person who clears a debt both fit the one word.

clue.text: Trails off — without question a mockery of justice

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece surrounds another
off means gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: how is a question word

explanation.surface: Trails peter out, leaving no questions to answer: justice mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is read as 'outside', not 'lacking', which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is staged for propaganda with the verdict fixed in advance, a sham of justice.

clue.text: Be hopeful Nick is on the organ

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal or take
the heart is the organ that pumps blood

explanation.surface: A man called Nick plays the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name but is the verb 'steal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be encouraged or regain confidence.

clue.text: Is an only alternative for an old European province

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement means the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A claim that a single region is the only other option.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyonnais was a historic province of France centred on Lyon.

clue.text: Camera may analyse housing saga of India

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A camera scanning and analysing an Indian epic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ramayana is one of the two great Sanskrit epics of ancient India.

clue.text: Akin to a judge's robes, pants?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word before it is treated as garbled

explanation.surface: A wry question: are a judge's robes really just underwear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like clothing beside 'robes' but signals the anagram; the 's after judge is a link standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'sober as a judge' makes the word a fair match for being like a judge.

clue.text: Capital broadcast sinned against capital's tendency to empathise with abductors?

parts.note: Stockholm is the capital of Sweden

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so these words are to be heard, not read

parts.note: sinned set against (next to) Rome, the capital of Italy; the s is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A news broadcast in some capital about a crime, with a comment on hostages who come to like their captors.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SINNED followed by ROME runs together into the second word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the psychological condition in which hostages come to sympathise with their kidnappers.

clue.text: Best rivals to compute creatively on Earth

indicators.note: on means placed after, so one piece follows the other
doing a sum creatively means rearranging it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A boast that one can calculate more imaginatively than anyone else alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To outcompete is to beat or outdo your competitors in a contest.

clue.text: Squid-like, powerless finger

indicators.note: without power means the abbreviation for power, P, is removed

parts.note: a pinky is the little finger

explanation.surface: A weak finger compared to a squid's limp tentacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid squirt dark ink, so being like one means being dark with ink.

clue.text: County town vehicle to drive home in reverse at that point

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in reverse means read backwards

parts.note: to ram something home is to drive it in hard
then means at that time

explanation.surface: Driving a car home backwards and stopping at a certain point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns RAM into MAR. Carmarthen is the county town of Carmarthenshire in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmarthen is the administrative centre of a Welsh county, so a county town.

clue.text: Dark sort of tales of a northerner and wrought iron

parts.note: someone from Norway, Sweden or Denmark

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of iron are reshaped

explanation.surface: Grim stories about a man from the far north and his ironwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought iron' reads as one phrase, but 'wrought' is the anagram signal working on iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the name of a genre of bleak crime fiction from the Nordic countries.

clue.text: Ten common moves of which I'll not speak

indicators.note: moves means the letters move to new places

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to discuss ten ordinary chess moves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock refusal to say anything about a subject.

clue.text: One's into lounge music that's sticky sweet

indicators.note: into means placed inside another piece

parts.note: to loll is to lounge
pop is popular music
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone slipping into a lounge where cloying music plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard, sticky sweet on a stick.

clue.text: See 10
Compel family to cycle (should not go out during major sporting event)

definitions.text: should not go out during major sporting event

indicators.note: to cycle means to go round, so the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Forcing one's relatives to ride bicycles, with an aside about a flame that must stay lit at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The torch lit at the opening of the Olympic Games burns throughout and must never be extinguished.

clue.text: Carted off to do some editing

indicators.note: off means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone carted away from the office to do editing work.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit text for publication, especially by blacking out parts.

clue.text: Ear inflammation aggravated, so it doubled

indicators.note: aggravated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
doubled means the word is used twice

explanation.surface: An earache that worsened, so it doubled in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' makes IT into ITIT; 'aggravated' then shuffles SO plus ITIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is the medical name for inflammation of the ear.

clue.text: Vein running through Tiepolo design

indicators.note: the answer runs through these words, taken from inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: A streak of colour passing through a design by the painter Tiepolo.
explanation.definitionFit: A lode is a vein of metal ore in rock, so the mining sense matches.

clue.text: The thing about politician high fliers is weakness

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: it means the thing
MP is a Member of Parliament
airmen fly high in aircraft

explanation.surface: A complaint that a politician's obsession with high achievers is a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: An impairment is a damage or reduction in ability, a kind of weakness.

clue.text: Tricky thing, being contra the speed of light

parts.note: contra means against, as does anti
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A puzzling thing that opposes the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful trick or caper, so a mischievous thing done.

clue.text: See 14
Rotating proton pen champion

indicators.note: rotating means turning around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A spinning pen used to track protons is praised as a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent supports or argues for a cause, as a champion of it does.

clue.text: See 6
Comic entertainer and where he often performed with balls

parts.note: seaside piers held end-of-the-pier shows with clowns
balls is British slang for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: A clown, his seaside stage, and his juggling balls.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pierrot is a sad clown in white; British seaside resorts had pierrot troupes on their piers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the stock white-faced clown of French pantomime, a comic performer.

clue.text: Toucan's migratory natural impulse

indicators.note: migratory means moving about, so the letters move to new places

parts.note: the word toucans, all seven letters, including the S

explanation.surface: A toucan's instinct to migrate with the seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Conatus is a philosophical term for an innate drive or striving of a thing to persist.
